# KCH SCO Orchestration

SCO composes sovereign sessions. It never creates a shared-context blob or reduces each chat to a project-wide prompt.

## Node contract

For every chat record native URI/ID, host, role, jurisdiction, memory boundary, authority, inputs, outputs, write set, state, terminal condition and handoff contract.

## Orchestration

1. Define the governing mission and decompose it into non-overlapping or explicitly reconciled functions.
2. Register existing chats without copying or fusing their full contexts.
3. Exchange bounded, provenance-bearing messages or artifacts.
4. Preserve local autonomy: each chat may retain distinct tools, memory, context and subautonomy.
5. Reconcile outputs through evidence and declared conflict rules, not majority vote or a global winner.
6. Persist topology, event ledger, unread cursors and resumable state.

## Difference from classic projects

A classic project shares a container and broad context. SCO instead supplies a graph of sovereign nodes, typed edges, selective transport, per-node authority, independent lifecycle and reversible membership. Grouping never implies fusion, inheritance or permission transfer.
